title: AI tells -- figurative verbs
description: A verb doing rhetorical work in place of an observation. The generated register reaches for a spatial or athletic metaphor where the literal relation was available: what something is, where it is, what it lacks.

rules.name: Name the literal relation
rules.message: figurative "sits": {match} -- write the literal relation: is at, rests with, is unused

examples.bad: The loader sits at the intersection of parsing and validation.
examples.good: The loader parses the file, then validates it.

rules.fix: Replace with the literal relation, or delete the sentence if it carries no fact.

citation.note: Disable for furniture or seating prose. Widest of the family (17 branches) because `sit` carries the most distinct figurative senses: position, idleness, discomfort, and priority. The nearest owned rule, `ai-tells-register.figurative-verb-verdict-core`, is a 10-token list about VERDICTS and does not reach any of these.

citation.note: Disable for gravity or accident prose. The membership branches (`falls under the category`) are the ones worth keeping in reference documentation: they are always a longer way to write "is".

citation.note: Disable for art or cartography prose. The `draws on` branch has the loosest tail in the family (`\w+` after an optional determiner), which is why it ships at warning rather than error.

rules.fix: Name the observation, then the doubt it creates.

citation.note: Disable for fishing, metalworking, or theatre-casting prose.

examples.good: The bug makes every retry reuse the expired token.

rules.fix: Name the effect, or the two things traded off and which one this takes.

citation.note: Disable for labour-action or percussion prose. `strikes a balance` is NOT covered: the source rule's noun list is note/tone/chord, and this port does not widen it. The loader's example check is what established that, after a first draft asserted the opposite.

rules.fix: State the dependency as a condition: X works only when Y holds.

citation.note: Disable for transit or equestrian prose. The `rides the <path>` branch is the one that fires in performance writing, where the literal mechanism (a cache hit, a branch taken) is always available.

examples.bad: The parser fails loudly on a bad header.
examples.good: The parser exits 2 and writes the offending line to stderr.

rules.fix: Say which channel it writes to and at what level.

citation.note: Disable for audio prose. `fails loudly` is the instance worth catching: it is a design claim with no observable in it, and the observable (exit code, stream, level) is what a reader needs.

rules.name: Name what connects and why
rules.message: figurative "resonate": {match} -- name what connects, and with whom

examples.good: Three maintainers said the argument matched their experience.

rules.fix: State who agreed with what, or delete the sentence.

citation.note: Disable for physics or audio prose, where the word is literal. Single token on purpose: every figurative use is the same defect, an agreement claim with no agreeing party named.

citation.note: Overlaps `ai-tells-register.figurative-verb-verdict-core` on exactly one token (`the point lands`); the other 21 branches, including the whole `is the move` and `what really matters` families, were unreachable by any owned rule.
